transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (BrightLane - Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (BrightLane - SRE), Anita Gomez (BrightLane - Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync for POC -> discuss rollout strategy, canary vs A/B, monitoring, runbooks, and outstanding security items before go/no-go. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Canary cutover plan and timing
- A/B vs canary evaluation criteria
- Monitoring, alerting, and dashboards for pilot
- Runbook and rollback steps
- Security: KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Next steps and scheduling final go/no-go

Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: yep hi everyone thanks for joining on short notice, i know we pushed the start a bit, uh quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya: hey this is priya, on from ml, good morning
[00:10] Tom: tom here, s r e, morning
[00:12] Anita: hi it's anita from security
[00:14] Marcus: marcus, se at redwood
[00:16] Alyssa: cool okay so agenda, go-live planning, canary vs a b, monitoring and runbook, then action items. we have about 50 minutes.

[00:40] Priya: quick status from our side, pilot qps has been stable, latency p50 around 120ms, p95 spikes to about 600ms on longer prompts. quality looks good, we found a couple of edge cases with multi-turn context though that we need to tune.
[01:05] Marcus: yeah we saw that in the perf runs too, kv cache isn't behaving as expected for the long prefix case, sometimes the kv cash is being dropped, so we're tuning the cache retention and sequence packing.
[01:30] Tom: just to flag infra, when you say p95 600ms is that hosted or dedicated? docs show those numbers were from hosted model variant, correct?
[01:40] Priya: hosted for the majority, we did one run on dedicated yesterday, p95 dropped to about 320ms but cost is notably higher.
[01:53] Alyssa: good to call that out — the tradeoff is expected. for rollout we need to decide canary traffic and thresholds for rollback.

[02:20] Marcus: proposal: start with a 5% canary on dedicated capacity for 24 hours, monitor latency, error rate, and token cost. if metrics are within threshold run 25% for 6 hours, then 50% for another 6, then full. fallback route to hosted variant if dedicated capacity degrades.
[02:45] Priya: sounds reasonable. what metrics specifically should we watch?
[02:50] Marcus: p50/p95 latency, 5xx error rate, queue depth on GPU pods, token cost per 1k, model output consistency measured by rouge/semantic similarity on sampled prompts. also memory pressure and kv cache hit rate.
[03:10] Anita: from security we need audit log retention confirmed, KMS key policies, and SSO mapping for service accounts. can we get explicit notes in the runbook?
[03:20] Alyssa: yes we will include a security checklist. marcus will add a KMS and audit log section to the runbook.

[04:00] Tom: about monitoring, can you share what the dashboards look like? we want per-route dashboards and synthetic checks. ideally ability to slice by org, route, and model variant.
[04:12] Marcus: we'll share a Grafana dashboard template — it has per-route latency histograms, error heatmaps, cost per token, and synthetic traffic monitor that hits core flows every minute. we'll also add alerts for p95 > 500ms or error rate > 0.5%.
[04:35] Priya: can we add an alert for semantic drift? like if similarity drops below .78 on our eval set?
[04:45] Marcus: yep we can wire up eval hooks and an eval-run alert. that's part of the quality monitoring.

[05:05] Alyssa: question on canary window timing, tom do you have preferred maintenance windows?
[05:10] Tom: we prefer off-peak, so 2am-6am local for us, but for canary we want a daytime test with on-call available. suggest 10am-2pm next friday for initial canary.
[05:25] Priya: next friday is fine, but we want at least 24 hours of data before bigger ramp.

[06:00] Marcus: operational details — we'll run scripted cutover steps: 1) enable route rules to send 5% to dedicated, 2) enable monitoring and synthetic checks, 3) verify model variant responses on small sample, 4) ramp per thresholds. rollback steps will be immediate route switch back to hosted and revoke any auto-scaling changes.
[06:22] Alyssa: and documented runbook will include contacts, rollback play, severity levels, and postmort checklist.

[07:00] Anita: on compliance, the customer asked about data residency for PHI — we need confirmation that logs are stored in region and PII is redacted. where are audit logs retained?
[07:12] Marcus: by default audit logs are retained for 90 days in the region tenant, longer retention is possible as an add-on. we'll note exact retention and KMS key region in the runbook.
[07:30] Priya: also need TLS enforcement and ability to rotate keys with minimal downtime.
[07:36] Marcus: KMS rotation is supported with key aliasing to avoid downtime. we'll show the rotation steps.

[08:10] Tom: can we get a smoke test matrix? we want a list of inbound requests and expected outputs for canary verification, automated.
[08:18] Alyssa: yes we'll deliver a smoke test CSV, and marcus will integrate into the synthetic checks.

[09:00] Priya: about A/B testing — we discussed using A/B for the quality signal, run models side-by-side. is that supported with current routing?
[09:10] Marcus: yes routing supports splitting by percentage across model variants. you can run A/B with a sample of traffic and collect semantic similarity metrics. drawback is higher cost since you double inference.
[09:25] Priya: we might do A/B for a short 8-hour experiment focusing on critical flows, then decide which model to push.

[10:00] Alyssa: timeline proposal: canary initial on 2026-03-12 at 10am (BrightLane time), 5% for 24 hours, then ramp on thresholds. final go/no-go on 2026-03-14. does that align with you?
[10:16] Tom: aligns, i'll reserve the maintenance window.
[10:20] Anita: security will aim to sign off by 2026-03-10 after reviewing runbook.

[11:00] Priya: one more thing on tuning — we need suggestion from redwood on quantization profile for the dedicated model to lower cost without harming accuracy. Marcus?
[11:12] Marcus: we ran a quick quant test: 4-bit quantization gave ~1.8x throughput improvement, small delta on semantic similarity (~0.02 drop). we'll include recommended quant profiles and cost estimates in the benchmark report.
[11:34] Priya: can you include sample prompts that showed regressions so we can review?
[11:38] Marcus: yes will attach the failure set.

[12:00] Alyssa: okay let's recap action items quickly — marcus will run full load benchmark and send CSV, priya to validate flows, anita to confirm security scoping, tom to reserve window, alyssa will send runbook.
[12:18] Marcus: i'll also push the grafana template and synthetic checks repo link.
[12:25] Priya: once we have the runbook we'll do an internal dry-run and report back.

[12:40] Alyssa: awesome thanks everyone, will circulate meeting notes and runbook draft by monday. final go/no-go scheduled 2026-03-12, we'll confirm earlier if any blockers.
[12:52] Tom: thanks all
[12:54] Anita: thanks
[12:55] Priya: thanks, bye

End of transcript.
